questions.question: If 4 * 7 * 2 = 361 and 5 * 9 * 1 = 480, then 2 * 1 * 3 = ?
questions.solution:
**1st Equation:**

4 * 7 * 2 = 361

(4 - 1) = 3

(7 - 1) = 6

(2 - 1) = 1

When concatenating these results (3, 6,1) gives 361.

**2nd Equation:**

5 * 9 * 1 = 480

(5 - 1) = 4

(9 - 1) = 8

(1 - 1) = 0

When concatenating these results (4, 8, 0) gives 480.

Similarly, 2 * 1 * 3 = ?

(2 - 1) = 1

(1 - 1) = 0

(3 - 1) = 2

So, when concatenating these results (1, 0, 2) gives 102.

**Hence, 102 is the correct answer.**

questions.question:

questions.solution:
**From dice 1 and 3** (from left to right) we conclude that 1, 6, 5 and 4 lie adjacent to 3. Therefore, 2 must lie opposite 3.

**From positions 2 and 3** (from left to right) we conclude that 1, 3, 2 and 5 lie adjacent to 4. Therefore, 6 must lie opposite 4.

So face which will be opposite to face ‘5’ is ‘1’.

Hence, the answer is ‘1’.

questions.question: The ratio of present ages of P and Q is 5 : 8. Three years later their ages will be in ratio 8 : 11. What is the present age (in years) of Q?
questions.solution:
Let present ages of P and Q be 5k and 8k respectively.

Three years later their ages will be in ration 8 : 11

Then;

(5k + 3)/(8k + 3) = 8/11

→ (5k + 3) × 11 = (8k + 3) × 8

→ 55k + 33 = 64k + 24

→ 64k - 55k = 33 - 24

9k = 9

k = 1

Present age of Q is 8 × 1 = 8 years

Hence, the correct answer is 8.

questions.question: A can do a work in 8 days, B can do the same work in 10 days and C can do the same work in 12 days. If all three of them do the same work together and they are paid Rs. 7400, then what is the share (in Rs.) of B?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can do a work in 8 days.

B can do the same work in 10 days.

C can do the same work in 12 days.

All three of them do the same work together and they are paid Rs. 7400.

**Formula used:**

W = E × T Where, W = Work, E = Efficiency, and T = Time

**Calculation:**

Let the total work be a units

Work done by A in 1 day = a/8

Work done by B in 1 day = a/10

Work done by C in 1 day = a/12

Ratio of work done by A, B and C:

⇒ A : B : C = 1/8 : 1/10 : 1/12

⇒ A : B : C = 15 : 12 : 10

Total amount paid to them = Rs. 7400

Share of B = Rs. 7400 × (12)/(15 + 12 + 10)

Share of B = Rs. 7400 × (12)/(37)

Share of B = Rs. 2400

**∴ The share (in Rs.) of B is 2400.**

questions.question: If x + 1/x = 17, then what is the value of frac{{{x⁴} + (1)/({{x²)}}}}{{{x²} - 3x + 1}}?
questions.solution:
Given: x + 1/x = 17

We know that: (x + 1/x)³ = x³ + (1/x)³ + 3(x)(1/x) (x + 1/x)

⇒ x³ + (1/x)³ = (x + 1/x)³ – 3(x + 1/x)

⇒ x³ + (1/x)³ = 17³ – 3(17)

⇒ x³ + (1/x)³ = 4862

To find: [x⁴ + (1/x²)]/x² - 3x + 1

Taking x common from both numerator and denominator, we get

⇒ x [x³ + (1/x)³]/x[x + 1/x – 3]

Substituting values

⇒ 4862/(17 – 3)

⇒ 4862/14 = 2431/7

∴ the correct option is 1)

⇒ 5(8 + a) = 80 + a

⇒ 40 + 5a = 80 + a

⇒ 4a = 40

∴ a = 10

questions.question: 15% of total time is spent on quality check and this time is equally taken from all other processes. So what will be the new sectorial angle (in degrees) made by total time of seats and glass?
questions.solution:
Since, 15% of total time is spent on quality check.

Percentage of time taken for quality check from all other processes

= 15/6 = 2.5%

⇒ Percent of time taken by seats = 6 - 2.5 = 3.5%

⇒ Percent of time taken by glass = 8 - 2.5 = 5.5%

⇒ Percent of time taken by both seats and glass = 3.5 + 5.5 = 9%

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice.**

He saw him conducting the seminar on personality development.

options.text: He was seen by me to conduct the seminar on personality development.
He was seen conducting the seminar on personality development.
He saw the seminar on personality development being conducted by him.
He saw the seminar on personality development to be conducted by him.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **‘He was seen conducting the seminar on personality development.****’**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let's understand this we the below example and rule-application:
 
• When there are **two** objects in an active sentence, there are **two possible active sentences and two possible passive sentences.**
 
• **Sentence 1**: *The professor gave the students the books.*
 
• **Sentence 2:** *The professor gave the books to the students.*
 
• There are two objects in each of the above sentences:
 
 
• **Object 1** = indirect object → the students
 
• **Object 2** = direct object → the books
 
 
 
• An indirect object is very often a person, a direct object a thing. When a direct object is followed by an indirect one, we put ***to*** in front of the indirect object.
 
• **Active sentence 1: "**The professor **(sub) + **gave **(verb) + **the students **(indirect object) + **the books **(direct object)"**
 
• Active sentence 2: "The professor (sub) + gave (verb) + the book (direct object) + to the students (indirect object)"
 
• Each of the objects (books/students) in the active sentences can become a subject in the passive sentence.
 
• **Passive sentence 1 (Personal Passive): "**The students **(sub) + **were given **(verb) + **the books **(object) **(by the professor) **(by-agent)**"
 
• Passive sentence 2: The books (sub) + were given (verb) + to the students (object) (by the professor) (by-agent)

• **Example: **The missing person's whereabouts were traceable through their phone records.

• **Changeable** (परिवर्तनीय): Capable of being changed.

 
 
• **Example:** The weather in this region is very changeable.
 
 
 
• **Inedible** (अखाद्य): Not suitable or safe to eat.
 
 
• **Example: **The berries on that bush are inedible and could make you sick.
 
 
 
• **Valuable** (मूल्यवान): Worth a lot of money or very useful or important.
